metadata.title: Comparative Analysis of Upwork MCP Documentation and Three Upwork Overhaul Plans
metadata.bottom_line: Use Claude v2 as the master plan, borrow a few execution habits from Gemini but not its positioning or timeline, and treat the MCP documentation as a working reference to verify against the live server. Claude v1 is superseded by v2 and can be archived.

document_summaries.summary: Technical reference for Upwork's official MCP server: job search, client vetting, proposal drafting and contract management from an AI assistant. Every write action produces a preview the human must confirm; accepting offers must be finalized on upwork.com. Defines a 5-stage proposal routine: fresh-job search, client vetting, check for an existing invite or proposal (error VJ-JA-10), draft, human confirmation.

Diagnosis: reputation is strong (Top Rated, 100% JSS, 20K+ earned) but the funnel is off (no proposals, 0 profile views, badge off, 2,172 USD in 12 months) and positioning targets a near-empty niche (OpenClaw, about 24 jobs in two quarters). Recommends repositioning around Claude implementation for businesses, an 85 USD/hr profile rate, a fixed-price ladder (Setup Sprint, Audit, Implementation, Care Plan), a DIY kit treated mainly as a delivery toolkit, and JSS protection rules.

Same plan on firmer evidence: exact counts (313 Claude-title jobs, only 9 allow 100+ USD/hr, 67% already have 20+ proposals), a comparable freelancer whose public history shows the small-job then expansion then retainer path, exact JSS weighting from the insights page (251+ USD = 1.25 jobs, 1,001+ USD = 1.5 jobs, 90-day repeat-client rule), and a new client filter: average hourly rate paid, not total spend. Lowers the rate to 65 USD/hr, adds an Automation Rescue offer, and puts past-client reactivation first.

Positions the profile as "Enterprise AI Architect" around custom MCP servers and LangGraph multi-agent systems. Keeps 120 to 150 USD/hr with a 3,000 USD contract floor. Proposes three catalog projects (MCP boilerplate 199 to 499 USD, custom MCP build 1,500 to 4,000 USD, feasibility audit 299 USD), 150 USD consultations, and a 7-day roadmap ending with 3,500 to 6,000 USD upsells.

agreements.point: The problem is activity and positioning, not reputation.
Move away from OpenClaw; the 24-job count supports it.

Fixed-price packages instead of a high hourly sticker. Visible history is 3 to 30 USD/hr, so 120 USD/hr looks inconsistent; packages hide that comparison (a 599 USD package delivered in 5 hours is about 120 USD/hr).
Start every new client with a small first milestone. The JSS base is only 8 eligible jobs, so one bad large contract could drop below the 90% Top Rated line.
Past clients first: costs 0 Connects and is the most likely week-one win. The repeat enterprise client is the first message.
Check the client's average hourly rate paid. Example: a client with 430K USD spent averages 5 USD/hr.
Remove claims a client could check and doubt: "8+ years" beside a 2017 to 2021 degree, and "100% GxP/HIPAA compliance".
Expect little from the DIY kit alone (median SKILL.md listing under 50 USD/month; 815 "Claude skills" products on Gumroad, most unrated).
Paid consultations, separated milestones, and written client confirmation that acceptance tests pass before requesting final approval.

disagreements.point: An "Enterprise MCP / LangGraph Architect" headline targets the thinnest part of the market: about 8 "MCP server" jobs in two months versus 313 Claude-title and 404 AI-agent-title jobs. MCP belongs in the title as a keyword, not as the whole pitch.

Not realistic. Catalog cash is not available in 24 to 48 hours (Upwork holds fixed-price funds about 5 days after approval); new catalog projects need Upwork review before going live; 3,500 to 6,000 USD upsells by day 6 depend on consultations nobody has booked yet; a DIY kit is not "zero maintenance" when Claude Code and MCP change monthly.
Repeats the mistakes Claude flagged: opens by challenging the reader and promises compliance ("Zero-Leakage", "strict healthcare, legal and enterprise compliance").

Selling a ready-made boilerplate on Project Catalog may break Upwork's rules, which as far as known expect services performed rather than resold files. Claude's framing ("a skills pack customized for your business") is safer. Verify the current catalog policy before listing either.
Day 7 asks clients for five-star feedback. Requesting a specific rating can count as feedback manipulation. Ask whether the client is happy and fix issues; never ask for a score.

Both titles are likely too long (about 81 and 88 characters; Upwork's limit is believed to be around 70, verify). Suggested: "Claude AI Implementation | Claude Code, MCP, AI Agents & n8n" (about 60 characters).

v2 suggests asking clients on the five idle 2023 to 2024 contracts to close and leave feedback. Closing now likely brings those contracts into the 24-month JSS window, and private feedback counts even if public stars look fine. Only ask clients you are confident were happy; offer the others new paid work (which also earns the long-term-relationship credit) or leave them alone.

65 USD/hr is reasonable, but the profile number matters less than implied because each proposal sets its own bid; it mainly affects talent search and invites. Recommended range: 65 to 75 USD/hr, with focus on package prices.
Do not spend 80 to 110 USD on Connects and Freelancer Plus on day 1. Past-client outreach and the open invite are free. Buy Connects once daily proposals start.

Reads like an AI-written summary with some errors: says proposals become "Pending / Accepted" after confirmation (confirmation only submits), overstates offer acceptance as a "cryptographic signature", and the 51-tool count is unverified. Use upwork__get_tool_help to check every tool before relying on it.
Both Claude plans note the connector is authorized as "Patrick H.", not Aryan P. Reconnect under the correct login before any automated step.

phase.task: Rewrite title, overview and skills using v2's structure, with the shorter title and the doubtful claims removed.
Set the profile rate to 65 to 75 USD/hr.
Reconnect the Upwork MCP under the Aryan P. login.
Verify two open questions: whether consultations are enabled (Claude says yes, Gemini says no) and eligibility for the Top Rated feedback-removal perk.
Add three portfolio pieces, including this Upwork MCP project and a Claude skills and connector setup built for your own company as a live demo.
Message 5.0-rated past clients, starting with the repeat enterprise client, offering the Setup Sprint.
Replace the two OpenClaw catalog projects with the Setup Sprint (299 / 599 / 1,200 USD) and the AI Operations Audit (750 to 1,500 USD, or Gemini's 299 USD version as a cheaper entry).
Buy Connects, then send 3 to 5 proposals per day in the 18:30 to 23:30 IST window.
Use the MCP routine with v2's client checklist (average hourly rate paid of 25 USD or more, fewer than 15 proposals, posted within 24 hours) and v2's proposal template.
Confirm every proposal personally before it is sent.
Offer full implementations (3,000 to 7,500 USD) only to clients who completed a Sprint or Audit.
Convert finished work into monthly Care Plans.
Build the skills kit as a delivery toolkit with a free sample on GitHub; treat sales as a bonus.

targets.checkpoint: After 20 proposals, if fewer than 6 were viewed, change targeting and the first two lines of the proposal.

limits.limit: No live Upwork data was re-checked for this analysis; figures come from the four reviewed documents.

Upwork title length limit, catalog policy on pre-made assets, JSS window behaviour for newly closed old contracts, and the feedback-removal perk are stated from general knowledge and must be verified on Upwork.
